title: Resolve partitioned ledger skew during rolling cluster resize impacting hybrid routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a rolling resize of Dedicated capacity (scale-up followed by eviction/handback across Dedicated and Private clusters), a subset of tenant ledger partitions were not atomically handed off. The partial handoff produced overlapping sequence windows for some sessions which the downstream billing pipeline interpreted as both replayed and new tokens, leading to a mix of phantom credits and negative invoice adjustments for a small set of customers using hybrid routing. This ticket tracks root cause, mitigation, reconciliation, and long-term fixes.

Observed symptoms:
- Customers reported sudden negative bill adjustments and then phantom charge corrections over a 3-hour window on 2026-03-03.
- Internal tracing shows session handoff RPCs succeeded at the control plane level but consumer shard applied partial segment metadata (start_offset mismatch).
- KV-cache rehydrate triggered replay markers that bypassed idempotency checks when partition ownership changed mid-session.
- Affected tenants were mostly on Dedicated pools with private backends that underwent node-level rolling resize.

Impact scope:
- ~9 customers with Dedicated capacity experienced ledger deltas larger than 10% of daily usage; 2 customers received negative invoice line items requiring manual credits.
- Real-time console showed gaps in hourly token rollups for implicated tenant shards.

Immediate mitigation applied (done 2026-03-05):
- Paused automatic rolling resizes for all Dedicated pools globally (hotfix toggle runtime-1.22).
- Deployed a fast patch to consumer shard that revalidates applied segment sequence on handoff and rejects partial-segment applies (PR #GITHUB/REDWOOD/PR/4231).
- Runbook executed to reconcile affected tenant ledgers and issue provisional credits where needed.

Root cause analysis (confirmed):
1) Non-atomic partition handoff: the control plane returned success after initiating handoff but did not wait for consumer shard write-confirmation when the target was on a Private cluster with different write-path latency.
2) Idempotency marker gap: the KV-cache rehydrate path assumes contiguous offsets; when a partial segment was applied, the idempotency bitmap was not updated for the overlapping range.
3) Billing pipeline tolerance: batch aggregation assumes monotonic token offsets per session; overlapping windows could be double-counted or subtract leading to negative adjustments during reconciliation.

Planned permanent fixes (acceptance criteria included):
- Make partition handoff atomic across control and data plane: introduce two-phase commit for partition ownership where control-plane success requires confirmation from target consumer (milestone: runtime-1.22.1).
- Harden KV-cache rehydrate to verify idempotency bitmaps and apply a safe-merge when gaps are detected; add unit/integration tests for gap scenarios (milestone: runtime-1.23).
- Add guard in billing rollup that detects overlapping offsets and routes suspicious sessions to a slow-path that emits a discrepancy alert instead of aggregating (console-alert + ticket creation).
- Backfill tooling: safe-backfill tool to reprocess token deltas for implicated tenants with audit logs and dry-run mode.

Reconciliation plan for affected customers:
- Run safe backfill for the 9 impacted tenants with dry-run results posted to the reconciliation dashboard (link below).
- Apply manual credits for invoices flagged as negative or inconsistent pending legal/finance approval; provide customers with a reconciliation report and timeline.
- Postmortem and customer-facing summary to be published by 2026-03-21.

Rollout/Testing strategy:
- Canary the two-phase handoff in a Dedicated staging pool that mirrors Private-cluster latencies.
- Introduce synthetic test that simulates mid-session partition reassignments and verifies no duplicate/negative token accounting.
- Add e2e regression in CI that replays historical incident payloads.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BR/ENG-988321+runbook
- Post-incident dashboard (internal): https://dash.redwood.ai/g/dashboards/incident/ENG-988321
- GitHub hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4231
- Two-phase handoff design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=89214421

Notes on trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Immediate block on rolling resizes (chosen short-term): lowest blast radius, available immediately, but delays capacity operations.
- Option B: Patch billing pipeline to ignore overlaps (rejected): hides root cause and risks missing other corruption types.
- Option C: Full transactional handoff (chosen long-term): higher implementation cost and some added latency on handoff, but guarantees ledger consistency.

Next steps (owner: Liam Chen):
- Complete two-phase handoff design review and prototype by 2026-03-18.
- Merge KV-cache hardening PR and add integration tests by 2026-03-20.
- Execute safe backfill for customers and finalize credits by 2026-03-22.
- Prepare customer-facing postmortem and coordinate with Customer Success and Finance for communications by 2026-03-21.
